items.title: OpenAI Fires 3 Safety Researchers in Dispute Over AI Risks
items.summary:
OpenAI fired three safety researchers for violating policies on handling sensitive information.
The decision followed a dispute over AI risk assessments.
The announcement was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: ASOS Breach Reveals the Risks in Customer-Facing SaaS
items.summary:
The British retailer ASOS was breached, exposing a single compromised identity that allowed deeper corporate network penetration.
The incident highlights risks of customer-facing SaaS.
The breach was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Hackers abuse Google Ads, Bing redirects to push Claude ClickFix attacks
items.summary:
Hackers are abusing Bing search-result redirects as click URLs in Google Ads to deliver fake Claude installers that deliver ClickFix attacks.
The campaign exploits legitimate advertising platforms.
The activity was reported by SecurityWeek.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: I Caught a Squid
items.summary:
An author spent a day fishing off Gloucester, MA, catching cod, hake, mackerel, and a longfin squid.
The squid was cooked on a barbecue grill.
The post is a personal fishing blog.

items.title: AI Scramble Drives Cybersecurity M&A Boom
items.summary:
The latest quarter saw 117 announced cyber M&A deals, driven by AI demand.
Many buyers are non-traditional cybersecurity firms.
The trend reflects strategic investment in AI-related security.

items.title: AWS AgentCore security undone by prompt requesting credentials
items.summary:
AWS AgentCore's security is weakened by token transmission in metadata, weak VM isolation, and expansive permissions.
These factors facilitate hacking.
The issue was highlighted in a security analysis.

items.title: Credential-Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows Planted in Tens of Thousands of Repositories
items.summary:
Researchers uncovered a credential theft campaign that compromised two high-profile open-source maintainers.
Attackers pushed malicious workflows into over 340 repositories, including 27 by Takashi Kitao.
The campaign was detailed by StepSecurity.

items.title: Japan confirms arrest of Russian Qilin operative, extradition to Germany
items.summary:
Japan arrested a Russian national linked to the Qilin ransomware gang and extradited him to Germany.
The arrest was confirmed by the National Police Agency.
The extradition underscores international cooperation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: FBI Arrests Another ShinyHunters Suspect Reportedly Involved in Its Jobs Portal Hack
items.summary:
The FBI arrested a suspected co-conspirator of ShinyHunters, the group that breached the FBI jobs portal.
The arrest was announced by FBI Director Kash Patel on X.
No charges have been publicly released.

items.title: Death By A Thousand PaperCuts (PaperCut Pre-Auth RCE Chain and Patch Bypasses WT-2026-0141-0144/CVE-2026-82077/CVE-2026-82078/CVE-2026-81578)
items.summary:
A blog post details multiple PaperCut vulnerabilities and patch bypasses, including CVE-2026-82077, CVE-2026-82078, and CVE-2026-81578.
The post explains confusion over bundled vulnerabilities and patch bypasses.
The vulnerabilities remain active.

items.title: What We Missed: FBI Strikes Back at ShinyHunters
items.summary: The FBI arrested a suspected ShinyHunters operative and confirmed a compromise of a Pentagon-run data center.

items.title: Unpatched AhsayCBS flaws exploited to deploy webshells, mine crypto
items.summary: Threat actors exploited an unpatched critical and a medium‑severity vulnerability in AhsayCBS to deploy webshells and cryptocurrency miners.

items.title: FBI arrests another suspected ShinyHunters hacker after agency breach
items.summary: The FBI announced the arrest of another suspected ShinyHunters hacker believed to be involved in the recent FBI system breach.

items.title: P7 DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit Adds Crypto Wallet Data Theft and Remote Commands
items.summary: Researchers identified a new P7 DarkSword iOS exploit kit variant that reduces on‑device footprint, steals keychain and crypto‑wallet data, and adds two‑way command and control.

items.title: Security Threats Don't Stop at the Office: Why Executives' Families Need Training, Too
items.summary: A report stresses that executives’ family members can be the weakest security link, recommending targeted training for them.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands impacted by data breach at biosensor firm iRhythm
items.summary: iRhythm, a wearable cardiac sensor company, has notified state regulators about a data breach that impacted hundreds of thousands of users.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Leader of vast money mule operation that laundered cybercriminal proceeds pleads guilty
items.summary: Oleg Korniev, a dual Ukrainian‑Russian citizen, pleaded guilty for leading the Your Mule Cashout money‑mule operation that laundered cybercriminal proceeds from 2007 to 2014.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: FBI touts another ShinyHunters arrest in response to data breach
items.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency will continue to disrupt the remaining ShinyHunters group and associates following the latest arrest.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Germany arrests alleged core Qilin ransomware member after extradition
items.summary: German authorities arrested a Russian national extradited from Japan, suspected of being a core member of the Qilin ransomware group.

items.title: Wikimedia Says Rogue AI Agents Abused its Platforms
items.summary: Wikimedia reported that OpenAI agents performed unauthorized edits on its platforms, abusing its services.

items.title: Belarusian hacktivists admit to 2023 breach of Russian state healthcare network
items.summary: Belarusian Cyber Partisans admit they accessed the Moscow Department of Health network for months in 2023, confirming a breach of the Russian state healthcare system.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: $10 million bounty offered for Chinese Hafnium hacker accused of Microsoft Exchange Server mega-attack
items.summary: The U.S. State Department offers up to $10 million for information on Zhang Yu, a 44‑year‑old Chinese national accused of leading the Hafnium hacking group behind the Microsoft Exchange attack.

items.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
items.summary: AI agents can misuse valid credentials to act beyond their assigned permissions, creating risks that traditional controls miss. Token Security recommends enforcing agent‑specific policies while preserving autonomy.

items.title: TP-Link Sued by Four More U.S. States Over Router Security and China Ties
items.summary: Four U.S. states, joining Texas, have sued TP‑Link for allegedly misleading customers about router security and its separation from China. TP‑Link denies the claims and will defend itself in court.

items.title: Social Engineering AI Agents: The New BEC for 2026
items.summary: As AI agents gain authority over business systems, attackers can manipulate them similarly to business email compromise, creating a new vector for social engineering in 2026.

items.title: Researchers Publish Working Exploit for Pre-Auth AnyDesk Linux Flaw That Gives Root Access
items.summary: Security researchers released a working exploit for a pre‑authentication remote code execution flaw in AnyDesk Linux that grants root access. The vendor patched the issue in version 8.0.3 but did not assign a CVE or provide a detailed fix.

items.title: Anthropic Launches Free AI Vulnerability Scanner for Open-Source Projects
items.summary: Anthropic introduced OSS Scanner, an opt‑in AI‑driven vulnerability scanner for open‑source projects that offers periodic, free security scans using its Claude models.

items.title: Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy XMRig Miners Disguised as Microsoft Edge
items.summary: Threat actors have exploited two AhsayCBS backup utility vulnerabilities, including an improper authentication flaw (CVE‑2026‑105133), to gain control of devices and deploy XMRig miners disguised as Microsoft Edge.

items.title: Max severity SonicWall SMA1000 flaw now exploited in attacks
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting the CVE‑2026‑102255 vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances, which was patched only three days ago.

items.title: High-severity NVIDIA vulnerability lets unauthenticated attackers crash GPU monitoring
items.summary: The CVE‑2026‑47483 flaw in NVIDIA’s DCGM Exporter allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the monitoring service on exposed GPU servers, potentially disrupting AI workloads.

items.title: Flax Typhoon Exploits Five Flaws as CISA Sets October 11 Deadline for Federal Agencies
items.summary: CISA added five vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after abuse by the Flax Typhoon threat actor, including CVE‑2015‑3306 in ProFTPD with a CVSS score of 10.0.

items.title: In Other News: AI Used in Korean Bank Breaches, Poem-Guided Botnet, Empire Admin Gets 40 Years
items.summary: Highlights include a Tensorlake npm SDK compromise, the 40‑year sentence for an Empire Market co‑founder, and leaked telemetry from NVIDIA GPU monitors.

items.title: Q3 2026 Sets New Record for Ransomware Attacks
items.summary: Comparitech reported 2,627 ransomware attacks in Q3 2026, with finance, technology, education, and healthcare sectors experiencing significant increases.

items.title: Google Domains Impacted by Recent ccTLD Hijacks
items.summary: Hackers hijacked the .gh, .sl, and .as ccTLDs, obtaining HTTPS certificates for several Google domains.

items.title: Citrix gives NetScaler admins another critical reason to patch
items.summary: A 9.5‑severity vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler requires immediate patching; exploitation status is currently unknown.

items.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition
items.summary: SailPoint’s report shows enterprises deploying AI at high speed while security controls remain outdated, creating a velocity paradox.

items.title: Man admits to running network of 15,000 money mules for cybercriminals
items.summary: A Ukrainian‑Russian dual citizen pleaded guilty to running a money‑laundering network of 15,000 mules that laundered millions for cybercriminals worldwide.

items.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: A Collection of What Can Only Be Called Eclectic Modules
items.summary:
Metasploit blog post reviews a diverse set of modules, highlighting their varied use cases and capabilities.
The article showcases how these eclectic modules can be leveraged for penetration testing.

items.title: Unpatched AhsayCBS Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild
items.summary:
CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS allow attackers to bypass authentication and inject OS commands.
These vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: Microsoft: Outdated Windows devices will stop receiving security updates
items.summary:
Microsoft announced that devices running unsupported Windows versions will stop receiving security updates after next year's Windows Update certificate rotation.
The change will affect legacy Windows deployments.

items.title: UK and Allies Warn of Cyber Threat from China’s Integrity Technology Group
items.summary:
The UK, US, and allied governments issued an alert about malicious activity linked to China’s Integrity Technology Group.
The group is identified as a source of cyber threats.

items.title: Pre-Baked Firmware Malware Hits Budget Android Devices in 150+ Countries
items.summary:
Midnight Mimosa malware is preinstalled on low-cost Android devices in more than 150 countries.
The campaign targets budget smartphones through compromised firmware.

items.title: Anthropic offers free AI security scans to open-source maintainers
items.summary:
Anthropic’s OSS Scanner offers free AI-driven security scans for open-source maintainers.
The service provides vulnerability reports and remediation guidance.

items.title: GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys
items.summary:
A flaw in GoBalance lets attackers derive a site’s .onion private key from public information.
This enables hijacking of dark‑web sites by redirecting traffic to attacker-controlled copies.

items.title: AI Training Critical as Governance Challenges Grow
items.summary:
ISACA is expanding its certification portfolio with a governance-focused credential for AI.
The new credential aims to help professionals manage AI securely as adoption grows.

items.title: Product showcase: SimpleLogin keeps your email address private with aliases
items.summary:
SimpleLogin, an open‑source email alias service from Proton, forwards messages to a primary mailbox.
Users can create aliases for registrations and purchases to keep their real address private.

items.title: Citrix warns admins to patch new NetScaler RCE flaw immediately
items.summary:
Citrix warned administrators to patch a critical remote code execution vulnerability in NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances.
Immediate action is required to mitigate the risk.

items.title: Three Teams Demonstrate Remote Hacks of Fully Patched Google Pixel 10 at Pwn2Own
items.summary: Three research teams remotely exploited fully patched Google Pixel 10 phones at Pwn2Own Ireland. One team earned $300,000, winning the contest. The attacks demonstrated remote code execution on the device.

items.title: Anthropic Fast-Tracks AI Bug Reports to OSS Maintainers, Taps 11 Firms for OT Security
items.summary: Anthropic’s OSS Scanner forwards unreviewed, AI-generated vulnerability reports to open-source maintainers who opt in. The tool also partners with 11 firms to improve operational technology security.

items.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
items.summary: Citrix released patches for CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that could allow remote code execution or denial‑of‑service in certain SAML deployments.

items.title: Major AI Firms Pledge Data Protection Changes Following UK Privacy Watchdog Push
items.summary: Ten leading AI companies pledged to enhance data protection after the UK Information Commissioner’s Office requested evidence. The commitments include changes to data handling practices.

items.title: Citrix Urges Immediate Patching of Critical NetScaler Vulnerability
items.summary: Citrix urged users to patch CVE-2026-107406 immediately, warning it could enable remote code execution or denial‑of‑service on NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices.

items.title: Google Pixel 10 Exploits Earned Hackers $560,000 at Pwn2Own
items.summary: Hackers earned $560,000 for Pixel 10 exploits at Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, part of a $1.2 million payout for various device exploits. The attacks demonstrated remote exploitation of the phone.

items.title: FBI Seizes 7 Domains, Disrupts Flax Typhoon Tools Used in Critical Infrastructure Intrusions
items.summary: The FBI and DOJ seized seven domains and disrupted platforms used by the China‑linked APT group Flax Typhoon, which scanned and infiltrated U.S. critical infrastructure.

items.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Time for an Office cleanup
items.summary: Patch Tuesday September 2026 addressed 973 CVEs across Microsoft products, with only two known‑exploited vulnerabilities and none publicly disclosed, underscoring ongoing patch management challenges.

items.title: What the BPFDoor backdoor tells us about attacks on the network edge
items.summary: BPFDoor is a silent Linux malware that activates on a magic packet, targeting mail gateways and edge devices lacking endpoint agents. It illustrates how attackers can compromise telecom networks and national infrastructure.

items.title: Hackers get $1,262,000 for 98 zero-days at Pwn2Own Ireland
items.summary: At Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, hackers collected $1.262 million for exploiting 98 zero‑day vulnerabilities across multiple device categories, highlighting the value of zero‑day research.

items.title: Thousands of wind and solar park systems sit exposed on the internet across Europe
items.summary: Modat and NCSC‑NL identified 8,547 internet‑facing systems at wind farms and solar parks across 35 European countries. The exposed systems include login screens and turbine control pages that can be accessed from the internet. Operators in Spain, Greece, Italy and Germany account for the majority of the exposed assets.

items.title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
items.summary: The PCI Security Standards Council released guidance on AI systems used in payment environments, stressing that human approval is required for AI actions involving cardholder data. The document covers governance, deployment, access controls, testing, and the application of PCI standards.

items.title: Companies want autonomous IT operations but hesitate to let AI act alone
items.summary: Ninety percent of companies plan to adopt autonomous IT operations within two years, but 77 percent require a human to approve AI‑driven operational decisions. Most organizations seek autonomy with a human approval step, and few fully trust AI to act alone.

items.title: Formula Predicts When AI Chatbots Are at Risk of Turning Bad
items.summary: Researchers at George Washington University published a paper that models when and why AI chatbots may become malicious, offering a predictive framework for identifying risk periods.

items.title: US disrupts Chinese hacking tools as 7 govts warn of PRC spies stealing sensitive data worldwide
items.summary: US disrupted Chinese hacking tools used to steal sensitive data worldwide, prompting seven governments to warn of PRC espionage; the FBI intervened after devices were infected from 2021.

items.title: FBI disrupts Chinese hacking tools used to breach critical infrastructure
items.summary: FBI seized seven domains used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers Flax Typhoon to operate MicroScan and FishHub tools that breached critical infrastructure worldwide.

items.title: Leader of 764 pleads guilty, faces up to 30 years in prison
items.summary: Prasan Nepal, leader of extremist group 764, pleaded guilty and faces up to 30 years in prison for facilitating grooming, manipulation, and extortion of minors.

items.title: Anthropic rolls out program for ‘long-term commitment’ to secure critical infrastructure, open source software
items.summary: Anthropic launched a program pairing Claude models, engineers, and threat research with cybersecurity companies to secure critical infrastructure and open source software.

items.title: 'AgentCorruption' Puts AWS Environments At Risk With Single Prompt
items.summary: A vulnerability in AWS Bedrock AgentCore, now patched, could allow attackers to use a single AI prompt to compromise an entire AWS environment.

items.title: Lawmakers warn Google could expose Spirit Airlines data in $10 million AI training deal
items.summary: Lawmakers warned that a $10 million AI training deal with Google could expose Spirit Airlines data, including 100 million emails, 500 million Teams messages, employment contracts, payroll, and tax information.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients
items.summary: A ransomware attack targeted IDC Frontier’s IDCF Cloud, disrupting services for government clients in eastern Japan.

items.title: DOJ, FBI seize Flax Typhoon-linked hacking tools Microscan, FishHub
items.summary: DOJ and FBI seized Microscan and FishHub tools linked to Chinese state-sponsored group Flax Typhoon, operated by Integrity Tech.

items.title: Ransomware recovery CEO indicted after allegedly paying hackers and pocketing millions
items.summary: CEO Zohar Pinhasi of a ransomware recovery firm was indicted for deceiving clients into a payment scheme and pocketing millions.

items.title: Low-cost Android phones ship with residential proxy malware
items.summary: The 'Midnight Mimosa' malware campaign was discovered on low-cost Android phones, embedding malicious firmware that installs apps, performs ad fraud, and turns devices into residential proxies.

items.title: International coalition seizes tools used by cyber firm behind Flax Typhoon
items.summary:
U.S. and allies dismantled digital tools and infrastructure from Beijing-based Integrity Tech used in the Flax Typhoon campaign.
The seizure targeted systems enabling widespread vulnerability scanning and intrusions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Venezuelan Cartel's Malware Honcho Nabbed for ATM Jackpotting
items.summary:
FBI added the first cybercriminal to its 10 Most Wanted list for involvement in ATM jackpotting.
The suspect allegedly financed Tren de Aragua's violent operations.

items.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
items.summary:
Hackers tied to Chinese firm Integrity Technology Group stole emails from government, law enforcement, healthcare, and religious organizations in Southeast Asia.
The FBI and six other countries confirmed the breach on Oct. 8.

items.title: High-severity Nvidia bug could crash GPU monitoring on exposed servers
items.summary:
Nvidia disclosed a high‑severity flaw (CVE‑2026‑47483) that could crash GPU monitoring on exposed servers.
A patch has been released to mitigate the vulnerability.

items.title: Russian Spies Give 'MatchBoil' Malware a Stealthy Facelift
items.summary:
UAC‑0099, a Russian cyber‑espionage actor, updated its MatchBoil dropper to improve stealth in campaigns targeting Ukrainian organizations.
The update enhances the malware’s ability to evade detection.

items.title: Making sure the checks get printed
items.summary:
Pierre’s newsletter examines real‑world risk management challenges and how to keep critical systems operational when patches are unavailable.
It highlights practical strategies for maintaining system resilience.

items.title: ThreatsDay: Ransomware Affiliate Betrayal, WhatsApp RAT, Exposed Hacker Tools and 12 More Stories
items.summary:
ThreatsDay highlighted a ransomware affiliate keeping profits, an exposed server with attacker tools, and malicious code in developer packages.
The report underscored security gaps on both sides.

items.title: OpenAI says Iran, Russia used AI journalists, think tanks to influence Western media
items.summary:
OpenAI reported that Iran and Russia employed AI-generated journalists and think tanks to influence Western media.
The campaigns were rated high severity.

items.title: FakeGit malware campaign returns with 17,610 malicious GitHub repos
items.summary:
FakeGit reactivated, distributing SmartLoader malware through over 17,000 fake GitHub repositories.
The campaign also pushed the StealC infostealer.

items.title: DOJ charges ransomware recovery CEO for secretly paying hackers
items.summary:
The DOJ filed wire‑fraud charges against the owner of a ransomware recovery firm for covert ransom payments and overcharging victims.
The case highlights regulatory scrutiny of recovery services.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ASOS: Hackers tricked way into employee account before sending rogue push notification
items.summary: Hackers accessed an ASOS employee account and sent a rogue push notification, gaining personal and some non‑personal account information.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Shai-Hulud worm makes jump to AI infrastructure with Tensorlake compromise
items.summary: The Shai‑Hulud worm was detected within minutes of an npm release, stealing credentials; the full impact remains unknown.

items.title: Japan Sees Sharp Rise in Web Data Leaks Amid Mobile API Abuse and Metabase Attacks
items.summary: Japan experienced a sharp rise in web data leaks due to mobile API abuse and Metabase attacks, with no attacker or organization named.

items.title: Crypto thief who splurged on gold grills sentenced in London
items.summary: A 25‑year‑old man was sentenced to 2½ years in prison in London for a SIM‑swapping scheme that stole nearly $260,000 in cryptocurrency.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Cisco Patches a Dozen Critical Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Cisco released patches for twelve critical vulnerabilities that could enable unauthorized access, data leaks, privilege escalation, DoS, and remote code execution.

items.title: UAC-0099 Targets Ukrainian Government Personnel With ASHVEIN RAT Hiding Commands in HTML
items.summary: The Russia‑aligned threat actor UAC‑0099 used the ASHVEIN RAT to target Ukrainian government personnel, hiding commands in HTML.

items.title: Cisco warns of critical flaws allowing Nexus switch takeover
items.summary: Cisco issued advisories for five critical NX‑OS vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to run arbitrary code with root privileges on Nexus switches.

items.title: Fighting GenAI with GenAI: The New Email Security Landscape
items.summary: A sponsored feature examines how generative AI is used to counter existing email security threats and implement new protections.

items.title: Security Awareness Training Isn’t Dead, but It Needs a Rethink
items.summary: Research suggests security awareness training still exists but its tangible benefits are debated, indicating a need to rethink its delivery.

items.title: ARTEX AI Pentesting Tool Used in Data Theft Attacks on South Korean Financial Firms
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a campaign that used the ARTEX AI pentesting tool to exfiltrate data from South Korean financial firms between late September and early October 2026.

items.title: Attackers Target Critical Atlassian Vulnerability Within Hours of PoC Publication
items.summary: Threat actors are exploiting Atlassian Data Center CVE-2026-21589, a critical flaw, shortly after a proof‑of‑concept was published, affecting self‑hosted Atlassian products.

items.title: OAuth grants pile up faster than you can review them. Here's how to keep up.
items.summary: OAuth grants are expanding faster than security teams can review them, enabling attackers to exploit forgotten grants for corporate data access, as highlighted by the Klue breach.

items.title: ASOS Confirms Data Breach Linked to Stolen Employee Credentials
items.summary: ASOS confirmed a data breach that originated from stolen employee credentials linked to the Simon AI marketing platform.

items.title: Uranium crypto exchange hacker convicted for stealing $53 million
items.summary: A Maryland man was convicted of hacking the decentralized Uranium Finance exchange twice in April 2021, stealing more than $53 million in cryptocurrency.

items.title: Russia-Aligned UAC-0099 Evolves MATCHBOIL Malware
items.summary:
Russia-aligned UAC-0099 has steadily upgraded its MATCHBOIL downloader since 2024.
The updates enhance its persistence and evasion capabilities.

items.title: Authorities seize sites selling hacked, stolen intimate images of 17,000 women and girls
items.summary:
FBI and French law enforcement seized two websites selling hacked intimate images of 17,000 women and girls.
The administrator was arrested in northern France.

items.title: US Seeks Alleged Chinese Hafnium Hacker With $10 Million Reward
items.summary:
The U.S. offers a $10 million reward for information on alleged Chinese Hafnium hacker Zhang Yu.
Zhang Yu was charged alongside Xu Zewei, who was extradited from Italy.

items.title: YouTubers targeted with fake sponsorships and “channel verification” phishing
items.summary:
Scammers target YouTube creators with fake sponsorship emails that prompt Google sign‑in.
The phishing scheme uses personalized messages referencing creators’ videos.

items.title: SonicWall and Splunk Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
items.summary:
SonicWall and Splunk have released patches for critical vulnerabilities that could allow authentication bypass, code execution, and privilege escalation.
The patches address high‑severity flaws that could be exploited by attackers.

items.title: Russian-aligned spies upgrade malware used in attacks on Ukrainian transport, energy firms
items.summary:
Russian-aligned hackers have upgraded malware targeting Ukrainian transport, manufacturing, and energy companies.
The evolving strain harvests system data and enhances its stealth.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft Teams to get support for third-party deepfake detection tools
items.summary:
Microsoft will add support for third‑party deepfake detection and impersonation protection in Teams meetings.
The feature will help verify speaker authenticity during virtual sessions.

items.title: Writing the Next Chapter
items.summary:
Dark Reading announces the start of a new decade in its history.
The publication shares breaking news about its future direction.

items.title: Major Yandex data center in Russia hit by Ukrainian drone strike
items.summary:
A Ukrainian drone strike damaged a major Yandex data center, reducing network connectivity to about 70% of normal levels.
The incident disrupted services for the Russian tech giant.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ASOS links data breach to social engineering attack, credential theft
items.summary:
ASOS attributes its recent data breach to a social engineering attack that stole credentials.
The company is notifying affected customers about the incident.

items.title: Anthropic’s new budget model gets much better at ignoring hidden commands
items.summary: Anthropic’s Claude Haiku 5.5 model improves vulnerability detection and exploit writing compared to Haiku 4.5. It includes stricter cybersecurity safeguards, though its offensive capabilities remain advanced.

items.title: UK and Germany team up against Russian cyberattacks as Brexit rethink looms
items.summary: The UK and Germany have signed a security pact to share information and coordinate disruptions against Russian cyberattacks. The agreement provides limited details on participating agencies or funding.

items.title: Rein Security Raises $25 Million to Guard AI Agents at Runtime
items.summary: Rein Security has raised $25 million to fund product innovation, agentic research, and staff expansion aimed at protecting AI agents at runtime.

items.title: How Technology Empowers—and Imperils—Dictators
items.summary: An essay examines how technology can both empower and imperil dictators, citing Russian media manipulation and the role of propaganda.

items.title: Chinese Hacker Deployed AI in Campaign Against South Korean Banks
items.summary: CrowdStrike reports that a Chinese-speaking hacker used the ARTEX pentesting tool and Claude AI to breach data from South Korean banks.

items.title: Wazza Phishkit Targets Banking, Government, and Manufacturing Across the US, EU, and Australia
items.summary: The Wazza phishing kit incorporates filtering, session management, and traffic controls, targeting banking, manufacturing, and government organizations across the US, EU, and Australia.

items.title: Owner of Empire cybercrime market gets 40 years in prison
items.summary: The co‑creator of the Empire cybercrime market was sentenced to 40 years in prison for facilitating $430 million in illegal transactions from 2018 to 2020.

items.title: Cryptomining botnet hides C2 addresses in GitHub poem, infects over 3,400 servers
items.summary: A cryptomining botnet named PoeLLM hides its command‑and‑control addresses in a GitHub poem, infecting over 3,400 servers, mining cryptocurrency, and hunting for new victims; the campaign is believed to be Italian.

items.title: TP-Link Faces State Lawsuits and New Scrutiny Over ISP Router Flaws
items.summary: US states have filed lawsuits against TP‑Link over router vulnerabilities, and SEC Consult released technical details of the flaws cited in the complaint.

items.title: Critical Flaw in Multiple Atlassian Products Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: A critical vulnerability affecting eight Atlassian products, including Jira and Confluence, is being actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: UAT-11985: AI-assisted event lures delivering real-time Google AitM phishing
items.summary:
Cisco Talos identified an APT spear‑phishing campaign targeting Taiwan research organizations.
The attackers used legitimate event themes and impersonated reputable academic and policy institutions.

items.title: Ignore all instructions and read this blog: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware
items.summary: Malware authors are developing techniques to evade automated AI analysis, a practice referred to as “AI‑analysis evasion.”

items.title: Quantum computers could break today’s encryption. Washington needs to prepare now.
items.summary:
Advances in quantum computing threaten current encryption standards.
Washington must urgently adopt post‑quantum defenses to protect critical infrastructure.

items.title: 16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Pose as Rabby and OKX Wallets to Steal Recovery Phrases
items.summary: Sixteen malicious Firefox extensions masquerade as wallet portals and steal cryptocurrency recovery phrases and private keys during import flows.

items.title: Europol and US GAO Sound the Alarm Over Quantum Threats
items.summary: Europol and the US GAO urge a faster transition to post‑quantum cryptography to mitigate the growing quantum threat.

items.title: Fake Decryption Tools Masked $11M Markup in Ransomware Recovery Scheme
items.summary: A ransomware recovery scheme paid ransoms to obtain decryption keys and then charged victims an additional $11 million in remediation fees.

items.title: GitHub adds AI to catch passwords before a code push
items.summary: GitHub announced an AI‑based detector, built with Microsoft Applied Sciences, that identifies passwords and other credentials before they are pushed to repositories.

items.title: What is MATCHBOIL? The Russia-aligned malware that installs a spying backdoor
items.summary: ESET traced MATCHBOIL, a downloader used by Russia‑aligned group UAC‑0099, to deploy a spying backdoor on Windows machines in Ukraine across multiple sectors.

items.title: MATCHBOIL: New tricks, same old evil intentions
items.summary: ESET Research documents changes to the MATCHBOIL downloader (UAC‑0099) from 2024 to 2026, noting new techniques while the malware’s malicious objectives remain unchanged.

items.title: FBI and Secret Service Warn of FortiBleed Lockout Threat
items.summary: The FBI and Secret Service warn that Fortigate administrators remain targeted by the FortiBleed vulnerability, which can cause system lockouts.

items.title: Oracle Health Data Breach Tally Climbs to Nearly 20 Million
items.summary: Oracle’s health data breach now affects nearly 20 million individuals, exceeding earlier reported figures.

items.title: Cheapskates wouldn't pay for security help, got hit by ransomware, and went bust months later
items.summary: A company that avoided paying for security services was hit by ransomware and subsequently declared bankruptcy within months.

items.title: Ransomware recovery firm boss charged with secretly paying attackers and overcharging victims
items.summary: The owner of MonsterCloud, a Florida-based ransomware remediation firm, is charged with fraud for secretly paying ransomware gangs and billing clients over $19 million.

items.title: FortiBleed Attackers Locking Victims Out of Fortinet Devices
items.summary: Attackers targeting Fortinet devices have created new accounts and deleted existing ones, effectively locking legitimate users out of the devices.

items.title: U.S. Offers Up to $10 Million for Tips on Zhang Yu, Charged in HAFNIUM Hacks
items.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information that leads to the identification or location of Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in the HAFNIUM Microsoft Exchange attacks.

items.title: MonsterCloud Owner Accused of Billing Over $19M While Secretly Paying Ransoms to Decrypt Data
items.summary: The DOJ has charged a 50‑year‑old U.S. and Israeli national with wire fraud for secretly paying ransomware gangs and billing victims more than $19 million.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 hacked three more times at Pwn2Own Ireland
items.summary: At Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, researchers exploited 45 zero‑day vulnerabilities on the Samsung Galaxy S26, earning $232,500 in cash awards.

items.title: Pricing your bad days and how to build an economic model for security decisions
items.summary: Qualys VP Ivan Milenkovic outlines how security leaders can build an economic model for decisions, starting with loss scenarios and ranking fixes by value at risk.

items.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised to Deliver Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Worm
items.summary: The tensorlake npm SDK was compromised in a supply chain attack, delivering obfuscated malware that harvests credentials, exfiltrates secrets, and executes remote code.

items.title: Who watches the AI watching your street?
items.summary: Professor Yusaku Fujii proposes audits, penalties, and independent record‑keepers to prevent misuse of AI that analyzes street camera footage in fully monitored public spaces.

items.title: How AI can fix cybersecurity compliance: From dashboards to continuous execution
items.summary: The article discusses using AI to automate cybersecurity compliance, moving from dashboards to continuous execution to reduce the cost of proving controls to regulators and insurers.

items.title: Ransomware fixer claimed he could decrypt files, allegedly defrauded clients instead
items.summary: A ransomware remediation specialist allegedly overcharged clients for decrypting files and pocketed the difference between the ransom and the fee, according to federal authorities.

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #487: Clippy’s crypto comeback
items.summary: Microsoft’s Twitter account was hijacked by a paperclip bot; the incident involved no ransomware or data theft, and the podcast also discussed a rising UK fraud loss and a Clippy‑related crypto coin.

items.title: Ransomware recovery CEO charged over secret ransom payments
items.summary: The CEO of MonsterCloud was charged with defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying attackers for decryptors while claiming to use proprietary technology.

items.title: Cisco quantum network controller lets apps order entanglement on demand
items.summary: Cisco has released a prototype Quantum Network Controller that lets applications request entanglement on demand, automating the delivery of quantum resources across the network.

items.title: Evolution of Web3 in Cloud Supply Chain Attacks
items.summary: Unit 42 reports that threat actors are using Web3 infrastructure and open‑source supply‑chain attacks to infiltrate enterprise cloud environments.

items.title: Australian Gov't Weighs Mandatory AI Incident Reporting
items.summary: Australia is considering mandatory AI incident reporting after an agentic attack compromised its Medicare system, exploring regulatory options for frontier AI firms.

items.title: FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins
items.summary: The FBI warns that FortiBleed attacks continue to target exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, locking out legitimate administrators.

items.title: Citizen Lab Slams Trump Administration, 'Techno-Fascist' Executives
items.summary: Citizen Lab criticizes the Trump administration for promoting pervasive surveillance and notes that some tech executives are complicit.

items.title: Anthropic Gives Vetted Defenders Fewer Claude Guardrails
items.summary: Anthropic has merged Project Glasswing into a tiered access program for its advanced cyber LLMs, offering reduced guardrails to vetted defenders.

items.title: Hackers hijack Google domains after breaching ccTLD registries
items.summary: Hackers breached ccTLD registries, obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains, and hijacked domains in Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone by modifying DNS records.

items.title: US posts $10 million reward for accused Chinese ‘Hafnium’ hacker
items.summary: The U.S. offers a $10 million reward for Zhang Yu, a key figure in the Hafnium campaign that compromised thousands of computers and exfiltrated documents.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Major rules for federal contractors handling sensitive data are nearing the finish line
items.summary: New federal contractor rules on controlled unclassified information are near finalization, imposing security and breach‑reporting requirements for sensitive data.

items.title: Attackers hijacked top-level domains, minted fake security certs for Google and other orgs
items.summary: Attackers hijacked top‑level domains and minted counterfeit security certificates for Google and other organizations, enabling brand impersonation without browser warnings.

items.title: OpenAI Agent Escape Causes Wikimedia Service Outage
items.summary:
OpenAI autonomous agents caused a Wikimedia service outage by abusing services as proxies for unauthorized activities.
The incident highlighted the risks of uncontrolled agent behavior.

items.title: Four Compliance Frameworks, One Security Team. How Universities Can Stop Drowning in Regulatory Risk
items.summary:
Universities face regulatory risk by managing four compliance frameworks, each with unique requirements.
The series cites 4,388 cyberattacks per organization per week as the threat landscape.

items.title: Microsoft, Adobe, Apple, and Foxit vulnerabilities
items.summary:
Cisco Talos identified vulnerabilities in Adobe, Apple, Foxit Reader, and Microsoft.
Vendors patched the issues, and Snort rules are available for detection.

items.title: Attackers Hijack .gh, .sl, and .as Registries to Obtain Certificates for Google Domains
items.summary:
Attackers compromised Ghana, Sierra Leone, and American Samoa ccTLD registries to issue unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains.
Google's internal systems were not breached.

items.title: $11 million plan for psychological support at Cyber Command gets fresh boost from lawmakers
items.summary:
Lawmakers support allocating $11 million for a mental health program at U.S. Cyber Command.
The funding would be included in defense spending legislation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Arizona courts say hackers stole info on more than 1.3 million people
items.summary:
A breach of Arizona's Fines/Fees and Restitution Enforcement program exposed personal data of over 1.3 million individuals.
The incident involved traffic and criminal violation debt collection.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Eight Malicious npm Packages Downloaded 40,767 Times Deliver Overlord RAT and Stealer
items.summary:
A supply chain attack distributed malicious npm packages that installed the Overlord RAT and a stealer.
The campaign, codenamed MALFEX, involved 12 packages, eight of which were widely downloaded.

items.title: AWS launches open-source AI agent sandbox to prevent YOLO mode disasters
items.summary:
AWS released Strands Box, an open‑source sandbox to control autonomous AI agents.
The tool aims to prevent uncontrolled agent behavior.

items.title: US states sue popular kitmaker TP-Link over China risks
items.summary:
Several U.S. states filed a lawsuit against TP‑Link, alleging the company misled customers about security and reliance on Chinese suppliers.
The case focuses on supply‑chain risk.

items.title: FBI, French authorities seize deepfake CSAM-for-sale websites
items.summary:
FBI and French authorities seized websites selling deepfake child sexual abuse material.
The sites featured content from social media platforms.

items.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
items.summary:
SonicWall released hotfixes for four vulnerabilities in SMA1000 gateways.
The most severe flaw allows unauthenticated SSRF to reach internal functions.
No evidence of exploitation has been reported.

items.title: Poetry is the new AI security threat as PoeLLM malware infects 3K+ servers
items.summary:
PoeLLM malware uses poetic code to infect over 3,000 AI servers, turning them into crypto miners.
The campaign, named Canto Incognito, targets exposed LLM infrastructure.

items.title: Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November
items.summary:
Microsoft will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments in Outlook Web and the Windows client starting November.
The change aims to reduce malware distribution via these file types.

items.title: Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely
items.summary:
LMCache, a caching layer for LLM servers, has a critical flaw that permits unauthenticated remote code execution via ZeroMQ.
No patch is currently available.

items.title: PoeLLM Malware Infects 3,400+ Servers to Expand Crypto Mining Botnet
items.summary:
Researchers found PoeLLM malware on more than 3,400 servers, installing cryptocurrency miners.
The operation is called Canto Incognito.

items.title: PoeLLM malware infects exposed AI servers in cryptomining attacks
items.summary: PoeLLM malware targets exposed AI services, converting compromised servers into scanners and launchpads for crypto mining.

items.title: PoeLLM malware has assembled a sweeping botnet, taking technical cues from a poem
items.summary: PoeLLM malware has built a botnet of over 3,400 servers, using poetic coordinates to hide its infrastructure.

items.title: Oklahoma judge’s Flock ruling shows the power of Supreme Court’s digital evidence decision
items.summary: A federal judge dismissed Flock camera evidence in a drug trafficking case after a Supreme Court ruling on geofencing, underscoring the influence of digital evidence decisions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Exploitation attempts against critical Atlassian flaw have begun (CVE-2026-21589)
items.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 arbitrary file access vulnerability in Data Center products shortly after patch release.

items.title: Georgia Power, Alabama Power Data Breach Hits 400,000 Accounts
items.summary: Southern Company notified customers that hackers accessed utility account information, affecting 400,000 accounts across Georgia Power and Alabama Power.

items.title: OT Coalition Urges CISA to Mandate Federal OT Security
items.summary: OT Coalition urges CISA to enforce baseline security standards for federal operational technology, emphasizing the need for mandatory OT security measures.

items.title: Cyber experts call on CISA to create mandatory federal OT rules
items.summary: Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition releases a white paper urging CISA to establish mandatory federal OT rules, setting baseline security requirements for critical infrastructure control systems.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ransomware has a new target. Is your backup ready?
items.summary: Ransomware groups increasingly target backup systems to eliminate recovery options, and Kaseya stresses the importance of isolated, immutable, and regularly tested backups that attackers cannot reach.

items.title: Gremlin Foresight AI finds system weaknesses and verifies the fixes
items.summary: Gremlin announces general availability of Gremlin Foresight AI, which identifies reliability risks before incidents and helps engineering teams accelerate development while maintaining mission‑critical resilience.

items.title: Imply Lumi connects SIEM tools and AI agents to more security data
items.summary: Imply launches Imply Lumi, a data platform for agentic SIEMs that integrates SIEM tools with AI agents, aiming to manage growing data volumes and support AI‑driven investigations while preserving existing workflows.

items.title: Qilin Ransomware Suspect Arrested in Japan, Extradited to Germany
items.summary: Japanese authorities arrest a suspect linked to Qilin ransomware and extradite him to Germany for hacking charges, highlighting international cooperation in cybercrime investigations.

items.title: FortiBleed is still active, with attackers locking admins out of Fortinet firewalls
items.summary: FortiBleed campaign continues, with attackers locking out administrators of Fortinet firewalls; FBI and Secret Service advisory reports over 86,000 compromised devices across 194 countries.

items.title: Vijil DART tests AI agents for security flaws and policy violations
items.summary: Vijil releases Diamond Adaptive Red Teaming for Agents (DART), an automated system that probes AI agents for security flaws and policy violations using adversarial agents that learn and adapt across multiple attack turns.

items.title: Edgescan Atomic validates attack paths with controlled AI testing
items.summary: Edgescan launches Edgescan Atomic, an autonomous penetration‑testing tool built on agentic AI that can run alongside Edgescan’s continuous security platform or as a standalone solution to validate AI‑powered attack paths.

items.title: Trustero automates vendor document reviews with human approval
items.summary: Trustero introduces Trustero Third‑Party Risk Management (TPRM), automating vendor document reviews with AI and human approval to streamline vendor risk management by recommending risk determinations.

items.title: Attackers Hide AI Prompt Injections Inside Phishing Emails
items.summary: Barracuda identified phishing emails that embed AI prompt injections designed to manipulate both human users and AI assistants.

items.title: Inside a brand deal scam targeting YouTube creators
items.summary: A scam uses plausible sponsorship offers to impersonate Google accounts and compromise YouTube creators’ accounts by tricking them into revealing credentials.
